_help: Journal entries, in order. Each appears once its 'when' is true: 'always', 'flag:<id>', 'ability:<id>' or 'room:<id>' (visited). The Songs page is added by the game.

entries.title: The winter
entries.text: Hades called Persephone home too early, and the seasons broke. Orpheus has sworn to finish a song that brings the spring back.

entries.title: Eurydice
entries.text: A drifter keeping the Hearth in the Frozen Grove. Hungry, sharp, and not impressed. She wants to hear the song when it's finished.

entries.title: Hearths and Words
entries.text: Press Up at a Hearth of Hestia to rest: full health, a save, and a Word. A Word is your whole game in a few letters. Enter it on the title screen to carry on anywhere.

entries.title: Olives
entries.text: Olives are money, even to gods. Dying leaves half of yours where you fell, guarded by your echo. Beat it to take them back. Die again first, and they're gone.

entries.title: Fighting
entries.text: X swings the club, C dodges (nothing can hurt you mid-dodge). Enemies attack on the beat, so the music warns you. A swing on the beat hits half again as hard and fills your Muse.

entries.title: Zeus
entries.text: Restrung the lyre with gold thread and taught the Song of Zeus. Sells Ambrosia (one more heart) for 30 olives. His advice: go east to Athens, and hit the bull from behind.

entries.title: Song seals
entries.text: Doors marked with a lyre open to the Song of Zeus. Stand close, hold the lyre (Shift), and play Up, Left, Right, Up. One is in the old temple, west of the Shepherd's Drop.

entries.title: Crouching
entries.text: Hold Down to crouch. Swing while crouched to strike low: the only way to reach a scorpion. Crouching also ducks under venom.

entries.title: The Colchis Bull
entries.text: A bronze machine in the pen under the brook. Its front is armour. When it scrapes the ground it charges on the next beat: dodge through it, or get up high. Dazed against a wall, it's open everywhere.

entries.title: The road east
entries.text: With the bull beaten, the gate east of the pen is open. Athens lies beyond, and Athena with it.
